summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and chronic hepatitis C was admitted for surgical management of malignant fibrous histiocytoma in the left tibia, diagnosed after an open biopsy following a non-diagnostic CT-guided procedure. She underwent wide excision of the tumor with intercalary prosthetic reconstruction and a medial gastrocnemius flap. The surgery was uncomplicated, and she recovered well with controlled pain, no signs of infection, and stable hemoglobin. She was transitioned to oral pain medications, advanced in physical therapy with weight-bearing as tolerated, and discharged home on postoperative day five. Discharge instructions included Lovenox for DVT prophylaxis, wound care, pain management, and follow-up with orthopedics and oncology.
problems: Malignant neoplasm of long bones of lower limb
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
